page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided via a 236 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-threaded scaling presents a notable tradeoff; the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET operations, consistently perform within the average range. Large-model LLM prompt processing is a bottleneck, registering in the bottom 10% for a 7B model, though text generation remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ads_v7 offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads that require high single-threaded performance without the premium cost of memory-optimized or compute-optimized tiers. The inclusion of 236 GB of local storage adds value for applications requiring temporary scratch space. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including light web serving, database operations with moderate IOPS requirements, single-threaded data processing tasks, and basic application hosting.
